facts.text: Northbrook’s name means “northern brook,” a literal reference to a stream that flows to the north of the town.
The first permanent settlement appeared in 1790 when Irish immigrant John Dunlap founded Dunlap’s Station along the Great Miami River.
German immigrants began arriving in the 1840s, bringing half‑timbered farmhouses that helped shape the area’s early architecture.
The Ohio and Mississippi Railroad reached Northbrook in the 1850s, turning isolated farms into a connected community linked to Cincinnati.
After World War II, Northbrook grew rapidly in the 1960s and 1970s with ranch‑style homes and cul‑de‑sacs built for returning veterans.
In 2017, Northbrook faced an economic downturn that included a peak of 61 overdose incidents, highlighting local public health challenges.
